Because the $\text{C-H}$ (or $\text{C-D}$) bond is cleaved in the fast second step, it does not influence the overall reaction rate. Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The most effective synthetic route to prepare pure n-propylbenzene from benzene is Friedel-Crafts acylation with propanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ followed by Clemmensen reduction, rather than direct Friedel-Crafts alkylation with 1-chloropropane.
Reason (R): In Friedel-Crafts acylation, the intermediate acylium ion ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-C}^+\text{=O}$) does not undergo carbocation rearrangement, and the carbonyl group deactivates the ring, completely preventing polyalkylation.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Direct alkylation of benzene with 1-chloropropane produces predominantly isopropylbenzene (cumene) due to rapid 1,2-hydride shift of the primary propyl cation to a secondary carbocation, alongside polyalkylation products. In contrast, acylation with propanoyl chloride followed by Clemmensen reduction ($	ext{Zn-Hg} / 	ext{conc. } 	ext{HCl}$) cleanly converts propiophenone to n-propylbenzene without structural rearrangement. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Propanoyl chloride and $\text{AlCl}_3$ generate an acylium ion ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-}\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{=O} \leftrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-C}\equiv\overset{+}{\text{O}}$) which is resonance-stabilized with a full octet on all atoms; hence, it does not rearrange. Furthermore, the electron-withdrawing acyl group ($-M$) deactivates the monosubstituted product against further electrophilic attack, suppressing polyacylation. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the behavior of substituted benzene derivatives in Friedel-Crafts reactions:
I. Nitrobenzene is strongly deactivated and does not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation or acylation, allowing it to be used as an inert solvent for such reactions.
II. Aniline fails to undergo Friedel-Crafts reactions because the basic amino group ($-\text{NH}_2$) coordinates with the Lewis acid catalyst ($\text{AlCl}_3$) to form an adduct ($-\text{NH}_2^+\text{-}\bar{\text{Al}}\text{Cl}_3$) that strongly deactivates the aromatic ring.
III. Phenol and anisole undergo Friedel-Crafts reactions smoothly in the presence of catalytic amounts of $\text{AlCl}_3$ without forming any coordination complexes.
IV. Benzenesulfonic acid and benzaldehyde undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation readily because their substituents are ring-activating.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) I, III, and IV only
B) II and IV only
C) I, II, and III only
D) I and II only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. The nitro group ($-\text{NO}_2$) is strongly electron-withdrawing through $-M$ and $-I$ effects, reducing $\pi$-electron density in the ring to such an extent that electrophilic attack by carbocations or acylium ions does not occur. Hence, nitrobenzene serves as a common high-boiling solvent for Friedel-Crafts reactions of other arenes. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Aniline is a Lewis base due to the lone pair on nitrogen. It reacts instantly with the Lewis acid catalyst $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form an acid-base complex ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-}\overset{+}{\text{N}}\text{H}_2\text{-}\bar{\text{Al}}\text{Cl}_3$). The resulting formal positive charge on nitrogen transforms the substituent into a powerful electron-withdrawing, deactivating meta-directing group, blocking electrophilic aromatic substitution. Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate Statement III. The oxygen atoms in phenol and anisole also form coordination complexes with $\text{AlCl}_3$, requiring stoichiometric or excess quantities of the Lewis acid catalyst, not merely catalytic amounts without coordination. Statement III is incorrect.
Step 4: Evaluate Statement IV. Both $-\text{SO}_3\text{H}$ and $-\text{CHO}$ are strongly deactivating, meta-directing groups that inhibit Friedel-Crafts reactions. Statement IV is incorrect.
Hence, statements I and II only are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Electrophilic monobromination of m-cresol (3-methylphenol) with bromine in carbon tetrachloride ($\text{Br}_2 / \text{CCl}_4$) at $273\text{ K}$ selectively yields which of the following regioisomers as the major product?
options: A) 2-Bromo-3-methylphenol
B) 5-Bromo-3-methylphenol
C) 4-Bromo-3-methylphenol
D) 6-Bromo-3-methylphenol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the directing groups in m-cresol. The hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) is at carbon-1 and the methyl group ($-\text{CH}_3$) is at carbon-3.
Step 2: Compare directing powers. The $-\text{OH}$ group activates the aromatic ring through strong positive resonance ($+M$) by donating its unshared electron pairs. This resonance activation is significantly more powerful than the weak hyperconjugative and inductive ($+I$) activation provided by the $-\text{CH}_3$ group. Thus, the $-\text{OH}$ group governs the regiochemical outcome.
Step 3: Evaluate positions activated by $-\text{OH}$. The $-\text{OH}$ group directs electrophiles to its ortho positions (carbon-2 and carbon-6) and para position (carbon-4).
Step 4: Carbon-2 is severely sterically hindered because it is situated directly between the $-\text{OH}$ and $-\text{CH}_3$ groups. At carbon-4, the position is para to $-\text{OH}$ and ortho to $-\text{CH}_3$; both groups direct incoming electrophiles toward carbon-4 cooperatively, and this position is sterically accessible.
Step 5: Therefore, electrophilic bromination occurs predominantly at carbon-4 to yield 4-bromo-3-methylphenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the reactions of benzene with chlorine:
Statement I: Reaction of benzene with excess chlorine in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride in the dark yields hexachlorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$) via exhaustive electrophilic aromatic substitution.
Statement II: Reaction of benzene with excess chlorine in the presence of ultraviolet light at $500\text{ K}$ without a Lewis acid catalyst yields benzene hexachloride (BHC / gammaxene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$) via free radical addition across the $\pi$-system.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. In the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ in the dark, chlorine reacts with benzene via electrophilic aromatic substitution ($S_\text{E}\text{Ar}$). When chlorine is supplied in excess under persistent conditions, all six ring hydrogen atoms are successively substituted by chlorine to form hexachlorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$) with elimination of $6\text{HCl}$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Under ultraviolet irradiation or strong sunlight at elevated temperatures without any Lewis acid, chlorine undergoes homolytic cleavage to generate chlorine free radicals ($\text{Cl}^\bullet$). These radicals add across the conjugated $\pi$-bonds of benzene, destroying aromaticity to produce 1,2,3,4,5,6-hexachlorocyclohexane (commonly termed benzene hexachloride, BHC, gammaxene, or lindane, with formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$). Statement II is correct.

Consider the following multi-step reaction sequence:
$$\text{Calcium carbide} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\text{red hot iron tube, } 873\text{ K}} \text{B} \xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCl / anh. AlCl}_3} \text{C} \xrightarrow{\text{Zn-Hg / conc. HCl}} \text{D}$$
The final major organic product $\text{D}$ is:
options: A) Ethylbenzene
B) Isopropylbenzene (cumene)
C) 1-Phenylpropan-2-ol
D) n-Propylbenzene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Hydrolysis of calcium carbide yields ethyne gas ($\text{A}$):
$$\text{CaC}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{HC}\equiv\text{CH}$$
Step 2: Passing ethyne through a red hot iron tube at $873\text{ K}$ causes cyclic trimerization to form benzene ($\text{B}$):
$$3\text{C}_2\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_6$$
Step 3: Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with propanoyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ yields propiophenone (1-phenylpropan-1-one, $\text{C}$):
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCl} \xrightarrow{\text{anh. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HCl}$$
Step 4: Clemmensen reduction of the aromatic ketone $\text{C}$ with zinc amalgam and concentrated hydrochloric acid ($\text{Zn-Hg} / \text{conc. } \text{HCl}$) selectively reduces the carbonyl group to a methylene group ($-CH_2-$) without affecting the aromatic ring, yielding pure n-propylbenzene ($\text{D}$):
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Zn-Hg / conc. HCl}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
